verdictStatement: This is the closest the ledger has come. Every one of my five v9 findings is genuinely repaired and I verified each by measurement: the four historical fold sentences now date the duplicate removal at v8 and one of them withdraws the old false language by name, claude2v6 is pinned at a digest matching the live file with the right verdict and finding ids, reMeasurementAtV10 is correct in all three values at the dispatch HEAD, idCollisionNote states the general rule, and v7Note is version-absolute. The append to reviewGuidance is a true append, the roster holds at twenty changed paths with zero escapees, and the contract itself is byte-identical to v9 across sixteen substantive keys — a fifth consecutive ledger-only successor. One thing fails, and it is the smallest finding I have raised in this lineage. The claude2v6 record added to close my v9 finding carries two advisories, CLAUDE-V6-ADV-1 and CLAUDE-V6-ADV-2, and they are classified in neither the folded nor the not-folded column; the string occurs exactly twice in the document, both inside that array. They are the only two of thirty-one recorded findings that resolve to neither column, and the answer is not inferable: one is satisfied by reMeasurementAtV10 and the other is only half satisfied, because the '/date is on this roster and is unchanged' disclosure that formed half of it is still absent. The pattern is the familiar one in its mildest form — the repair adds the record and leaves the accounting for that record undone — and it is two lines from closed.

coordinatorNote: REJECT of the artifact, not a disposition of the row. DR-101 stays OPEN at file 08 line 283, nothing here mints D-096 (A) or any owner grant, and no implementation is authorized. I want the shape of this verdict to be legible, because it is a REJECT on one two-line omission and that could be read as harsher than it is. The design contract has been untouched and correct for five versions and I re-derived it from live bytes again rather than inheriting the result. Every v9 finding, mine and Codex's, is properly repaired, and one repair is better than what I asked for — honestyRepairsFromV5[2] withdraws its earlier false language by name instead of quietly rewriting it, which is the right instinct and worth keeping. The single finding is that the record added to fix my last finding brought two advisories nobody classified. Add one notFolded line and one honestyRepairsFromV6 line and, on my measurement, this artifact carries zero blockers and zero SHOULD-FIX. Two smaller things I would fold into the same edit rather than a further round: the DCIC-V9-S2 narration says both Codex advisories were removed from notFoldedThisSuccessor when only DCIC-V6-A1 was ever on it, and the newly generalized id rule was adopted without conforming the six CODEX-V<n>-* entries that still contradict it — that split is why S-1 is hard to spot mechanically. Finally, two scope facts the coordinator should weigh: this dispatch narrowed my read set to the files it names, so unlike earlier rounds I did not open the Codex v6, v7 or v9 verdicts and I take no position on whether DCIC-V6-A1 and DCIC-V7-A1 are substantively satisfied; and the Claude v6 verdict is still the lineage's only review at mode 0644 rather than sealed 0444, which is worth resolving now that v10 pins it.
